title: SkiaSharp unification and the WPF host control

adr001.decision: Unify on SkiaSharp 4.154.0 and retire SkiaSharp.Svg in favour of Svg.Skia

probe.result: Build succeeded; runtime output: skia-version 4.154.0.0, picture ok, pixel #ff0b6e4f, rendered True

adr001.finding: Svg.Skia 5.2.3 restores and references against SkiaSharp 4.154.0 without a version conflict, parses an SVG and paints the exact expected pixel.

probeA.result: Build succeeded, 0 errors, but NU1701: SkiaSharp.Views.WPF 4.154.0 was restored using .NETFramework 4.6.1–4.8.1 assets, not the net10.0-windows target. OpenTK 3.3.1 / OpenTK.GLWpfControl 3.3.0 arrive with the same warning.

probeB.result: Runtime output: skia 4.154.0.0, bitmap 64x64 Bgra32, fallback-host ok

adr002.decision: Do not use SkiaSharp.Views.WPF. Implement SkiaViewSurfaceHost as SKSurface/SKBitmap -> WriteableBitmap -> Image, refreshed on ViewSurface.Invalidated.
adr002.reason: The only .NET WPF asset for this package is .NET Framework; running net4x WPF assemblies inside a net10.0 host is an unquantified runtime risk, and the package drags OpenTK. The managed fallback needs no extra package and was proven at runtime.
adr002.impact: VSB-01 stays as specified (Draw / Invalidated / HandleMouse* / HandleKey / HandlePinch) but the implementation is WriteableBitmap-based, not SKElement-based. No other feature changes.

limits: The probes run outside the desktop solution; they prove package compatibility and the render path, not the final control's input forwarding or performance.
Only one SVG was rendered; complex gradients/patterns were not exercised.
ADR-008 (how OilandGasTools is consumed) remains open and still blocks STG-15.
